item_name: Chinese-language and Chinese-group research on fly or insect vision for target tracking
bibliography: Search scope: Chinese queries (果蝇视觉 小目标运动检测 仿生 模型 跟踪; 仿生 昆虫视觉 目标跟踪 遮挡 果蝇) and English queries on Guangzhou University (Hongxin Wang, Jigen Peng, Shigang Yue, Mingshuo Xu, Qinbing Fu) and Institute of Biophysics CAS (Aike Guo). Chinese-language queries returned no Chinese-language primary paper on fly-inspired target tracking with occlusion; the relevant Chinese-group output is English-language and concentrated at the Machine Life and Intelligence Research Center, Guangzhou University (with University of Lincoln). Excluded per task: Wu-Guo 2023, vSTMD 2501.13054, Wang 2104.13018; Fu-Yue 2007.00886 (Biol Cybern 2020, DOI 10.1007/s00422-020-00841-x) is already covered in the project list and in item 'Small target motion detection lineage', so it is not counted as new (re-checked only: 30 fps synthetic stimuli, hand-set parameters, no quantitative metric, no occlusion/absence tests). New primary sources examined: (S1) Hongxin Wang, Zhiyan Zhong, Fang Lei, Xiaohua Jing, Jigen Peng, Shigang Yue. 'Spatio-Temporal Feedback Control of Small Target Motion Detection Visual System'. arXiv 2211.10128 v1 (18 Nov 2022), header 'IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems'; https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10128 , PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.10128 . A University of Leicester repository record (figshare 25209551, posted 2024-02-13) lists the same authors minus Jing under the title 'Bio-Inspired Small Target Motion Detection With Spatio-Temporal Feedback in Natural Scenes' - likely the published version of the same study (duplicate), journal and DOI not confirmed [uncertain]. No code link found. (S2) Jun Ling, Hongxin Wang, Mingshuo Xu, Hao Chen, Haiyang Li, Jigen Peng. 'Mathematical study of neural feedback roles in small target motion detection'. Frontiers in Neurorobotics 16:984430, 20 Sep 2022, DOI 10.3389/fnbot.2022.984430, PMC9530796, PMID 36203523; Guangzhou University and University of Lincoln. Supplementary PDF and ZIP (Data_Sheet_1.ZIP, 22.1 MB) on the journal page; no code repository cited. (S3) Hongxin Wang, Jigen Peng, Xuqiang Zheng, Shigang Yue. 'A Robust Visual System for Small Target Motion Detection Against Cluttered Moving Backgrounds' (STMD+). IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, DOI 10.1109/TNNLS.2019.2910418 (accepted 5 Apr 2019; issue year 2020 [uncertain]); preprint arXiv 1904.04363 (duplicate of the same study); code https://github.com/wanghongxin/STMD-Plus ; real data STNS dataset https://figshare.com/articles/STNS_Dataset/4496768 . Related but not examined in full: Wang, Peng, Fu, Wang, Yue 'Visual cue integration for small target motion detection in natural cluttered backgrounds' arXiv 1903.07546 (STMD + LPTC integration, precursor of S1); time-delay feedback STMD arXiv 2001.05846 (precursor of S2). Not Chinese-group, noted only: Liu Ziyin, Yifei Lu, Borst, Dorkenwald, Poggio, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.09.17.752514 (24 Sep 2026), connectome-based figure-ground via vCH presynaptic shunting on T4 terminals (abstract only). No 2023-2026 Guangzhou paper on occlusion or multi-target identity was found.
full_text_checked: S1: full text read from the arXiv PDF (14 pages, text extracted locally): method, Table I parameters, sensitivity study, datasets, metrics, Figs. 14-17, conclusion; journal version not accessed (Leicester record returned HTTP 403). S2: full text on PMC read up to ~100k of 110k characters (methods, datasets, metrics, results, data availability); last ~10k characters (end of discussion/references) and supplementary ZIP not read. S3: full text via ar5iv HTML (methods, Tables I-III, Figs. 13-21); GitHub code repository existence taken from the paper link, code files not opened [uncertain]. Chinese-language CNKI/Wanfang full texts were not accessible; no Chinese-language primary source was examined.
task_and_output: All three are detection, not tracking-by-identity. S1: small target motion detection; output is a per-pixel STMD response map thresholded into detected positions per frame; a second (LPTC) subnetwork outputs background motion direction/velocity via population (ensemble) coding that is fed back. S2: same task; output STMD response map and detected positions; contribution is a mathematical analysis (existence/uniqueness of solutions) of a time-delay feedback loop STMD -> lamina LMC. S3 (STMD+): detection of small moving targets with rejection of 'fake features' (small-target-like background patches); output is STMD detections plus a per-trace standard deviation of directional contrast recorded by a mushroom-body-like module, used as a binary target/fake decision. None outputs a bounding box, identity, presence score for a specific exemplar, or velocity of a selected target (S1 encodes background velocity only).
data_and_independent_videos: S1: Vision Egg synthetic clips (natural background images with rendered small targets, 200x200 to 500x500 px, 1000 fps; single-target groups varying target size, luminance, velocity, background velocity and direction; multi-target clips with 3, 4, 5 targets) and RIST real dataset (21 GoPro clips, 480x270 px, 240 fps, targets 3x3 to 15x15 px); only 6 RIST videos 'randomly selected' were evaluated (GX010220, 241, 285, 290, 300, 315). S2: Vision Egg synthetic (300x250 px, 1000 Hz) and RIST described as 16 GoPro Hero 6 videos at 240 fps, of which 3 were evaluated (GX010303, 335, 241). S3: Vision Egg synthetic (500x250 px, 1000 Hz) and STNS real dataset (25 videos), 6 evaluated (STNS-4, 15, 16, 18, 22, 25). There is no train/test split because nothing is learned; parameters were hand-tuned on the same kind of synthetic data and partly reused from earlier papers of the group, so 'unseen' only in the weak sense that real videos were not used for fitting [uncertain whether real videos influenced tuning].
target_size_and_input_resolution: Input is full camera frames, one 'ommatidium' per pixel (grey). S1: 200x200-500x500 synthetic, 480x270 real; default target 5x5 px, tested 1x1 to >20x20 px; STMD detection rate stays high to 15x15 px and drops sharply above (Fig. 15b); STMD response peaks at width 10 px / height 5 px (Fig. 6). S2: 300x250; default 5x5 px, tested 1x1 to 11x11 px (Table 2). S3: 500x250; default 5x5 px; lateral inhibition deliberately suppresses large objects. In all three the design target is 1-15 px, i.e. a few receptors, much smaller relative to the field than our targets (~9x12 lattice steps inside a 721-hexal crop that fills a large part of the eye).
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Synthetic 1000 fps in S1-S3; real 240 fps (RIST) in S1/S2; STNS frame rate not given in S3. Background motion is simulated by translating the background image (S1 velocities 50-750 px/s, S2 50-180 px/s, S3 background speed and direction groups); RIST contains sudden camera movement, shadows, weather and illumination changes but no dedicated camera-motion analysis. Temporal filters (Gamma kernels, tau in ms-scale samples) are tuned for 240-1000 Hz; no run at 25-30 Hz is reported (Fu-Yue 2007.00886, already covered, is the only group paper at 30 fps).
detector_and_exemplar: No learned detector and no exemplar in any source. Targets are whatever local maxima of the hand-designed STMD map pass a threshold; there is no notion of 'the previous target' or a template. S3's mushroom-body module keeps a motion trace per detected candidate (position history) and accumulates directional contrast along it - the only element resembling a per-track state.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: None; all hand-designed. S1: Table I lists fixed parameters (sigma1=1; n1=2, tau1=3, n2=6, tau2=9; n3=5, tau3=25; feedback alpha=0.1, n4=6, tau4=12) plus LPTC parameters (correlation distance beta, order n5, time constant tau5) chosen via a sensitivity study (Sec. IV-B, Figs. 6-8). S2: feedback constant a and Gamma kernel n4=5, tau4=10 (Table 1); smaller a gave better detection (Fig. 12A). S3: motion-pathway parameters from earlier work, contrast-pathway parameters 'tuned empirically'; the fake-feature SD threshold value is not reported. No loss function in any paper.
controls_seeds_splits: S1: ablation without feedback / with time-delay feedback / with spatio-temporal feedback on medulla and STMD outputs (Fig. 14); baselines ESTMD, DSTMD, Time-Delay Feedback STMD with parameters copied from their papers; no deep-learning or engineering tracker baseline; deterministic model, no seeds, no confidence intervals; real-video evaluation on 6 of 21 clips. S2: ablation over feedback constant a; baselines ESTMD and DSTMD; 3 real videos; no seeds or intervals. S3: contrast pathway on/off (Table II, Figs. 15, 17), SD sample count m (Fig. 18); baselines ESTMD, DSTMD; 6 STNS videos; no seeds or intervals. No random/shuffled-network control is applicable (no connectome); no matched-compute learned baseline.
metrics_and_numbers: Common metrics: detection rate DR = true positives / actual targets; false alarm rate FA = false positives / number of frames; a detection is correct within 5 px of ground truth; ROC = DR versus FA over thresholds. S1 (arXiv 2211.10128): multi-target synthetic, at FA=5 the spatio-temporal feedback model reaches DR=1, 'improvements by a margin of 14 percent over the Time-Delay Feedback, 32 percent over the ESTMD, and 40 percent over the DSTMD' (Sec. IV-E-2, Fig. 16a); single-target groups: DR close to 1 for target size 1x1-15x15 px, sharp drop above 15x15 (Fig. 15b), slight decrease for background velocity below 150 px/s (Fig. 15e-f); real RIST: best ROC on all 6 videos, values only in plots (Fig. 17); velocity estimation of background reliable within [150, 750] px/s (Sec. IV-C). S2 (Frontiers 2022): FSTMD above ESTMD/DSTMD at all FA on the initial sequence (Fig. 11B) and across backgrounds with 1 and 3 targets (Fig. 13) and on 3 real videos (Fig. 14); inhibition percentages of feedback: 2.7% for a fast target at x=198 versus 79.1%, 37.5%, 51.8% for slow background false targets at x=41, 54, 248 (Fig. 10B); advantage grows for target velocity above 200 px/s (Fig. 12B-F at FA=15); exact DR numbers only in plots; the introduction contains a sentence ('unable to improve the detection performance') contradicting the results, apparently a drafting error. S3 (TNNLS, arXiv 1904.04363): Table II, with versus without contrast pathway: at beta=150 DR 0.85 in both, FA 27.70 -> 0; at beta=450 DR 0.50 in both, FA 6.88 -> 0; Table III (m=1000 samples): directional-contrast SD 31.29-42.86 for the real target versus 1.38-3.88 for fake features; Fig. 18: SD needs about 200 samples to stabilise; Figs. 19-21: best ROC on synthetic groups and on all 6 STNS videos (plots only).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: not applicable in the learning sense; real videos were held out from parameter fitting only implicitly (S1, S2, S3) [uncertain]. Target absence (frames or clips with no target, refusal): no in all three; FA counts false positives per frame but no target-absent sequences are reported. Similar distractors: partially - S3 tests static small-target-like background features (fake features) and rejects them; S1 and S2 test background false positives moving with the background; none tests a second moving object of the same appearance that must not be confused with the target. Multiple targets: yes, S1 (3-5 targets) and S2 (3 targets), but as independent detections without identity. Occlusion: no in all three (also not found in any Guangzhou STMD paper searched). Night or low light: no dedicated test; S1/RIST includes illumination variation and shadows; low target luminance tested synthetically in S1-S3. Sequential operation on own predictions: no tracker loop; feedback loops are internal to the network (S1, S2), S3 accumulates along its own detected traces.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanisms: (1) S1 spatio-temporal feedback - a wide-field LPTC-like subnetwork estimates background motion direction and velocity by an ensemble of correlators with overlapping velocity tuning; this background-motion estimate is mixed with the STMD output and fed back negatively to the STMD inputs (medulla level), so responses that move like the background are suppressed recurrently while independently moving small objects are slightly enhanced (Fig. 14). (2) S2 time-delay feedback - STMD output convolved with a Gamma delay kernel and scaled by a constant is subtracted at the lamina LMC level; because of the delay it suppresses slow features (background clutter) much more than fast targets (2.7% vs 37.5-79.1% inhibition, Fig. 10B); the paper proves the loop has a unique bounded solution. (3) S3 STMD+ - a contrast pathway computes directional contrast at each candidate; a mushroom-body-like memory keeps each candidate's motion trace and computes the standard deviation of directional contrast along it; a real target moving relative to the background has high SD, a background patch that only looks like a target has low SD; thresholding SD removes fake features (FA 27.70 -> 0 at unchanged DR, Table II). Proposed modification (ours, not published): use the FlyVis wide-field pooled T4/T5 response as the background-motion estimate and feed it back as a delayed subtractive gain on the FlyVis photoreceptor/lamina input inside the crop (S1/S2 analogue), so that the core itself separates object motion from crop/background motion before the readout.
transfer_limits: 1) Frame rate: all temporal kernels and the delay feedback are tuned at 240-1000 Hz; at 30 Hz the same targets jump several pixels per frame and the delay/velocity tuning (S1 reliable background velocity 150-750 px/s at 1000 fps) does not transfer; S3's SD needs ~200 samples, i.e. ~0.2 s at 1000 Hz but ~6.7 s at 30 Hz, longer than a typical loss episode. 2) Target scale: designed for 1-15 px targets with lateral inhibition against large objects; our targets are ~9x12 lattice steps in a 721-hexal crop that is itself scaled to about twice the target, so targets are 'large' for STMD and would be suppressed. 3) Moving and rescaling crop: the background motion in S1/S2 is a translating image; our crop recentres and rescales each step, creating artificial global motion and expansion that the LPTC estimate would read as background motion. 4) Identity: none of the sources selects a specific previous target among similar moving neighbours or refuses when it is absent - they detect all small movers; S3 rejects static look-alikes, not moving look-alikes, so the core Z13 failure (choosing among similar neighbours) is not addressed. 5) Evidence scale: 3-6 real clips per paper, ROC only in plots, no seeds or intervals - far below the per-video bootstrap standard of our stand. 6) Environment: YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA already handle detection of all objects; an STMD detection map adds nothing unless it changes the choice or the refusal at association time. 7) Grey input: compatible (all three use luminance only).
research_questions_addressed: Q1: caution/negative - the main Chinese-group line (Guangzhou STMD) has no exemplar-based identification among similar targets and no target-absence tests; S3 provides a design analogy for refusal by trace consistency (reject candidates whose contrast history is inconsistent with an independently moving object) but only against static fakes. Q2: weak design analogy - S1/S2 ablations (no feedback vs feedback) show that changing a dynamics node of a fixed hand-designed core changes false positives at constant readout, i.e. a core-level fix; no probe separating representation from readout. Q3: direct caution - mechanisms verified only at 240-1000 Hz, targets 1-15 px, translating backgrounds; none at 25-30 Hz with targets >5 facets except the already-covered Fu-Yue 2007.00886 (30 fps, qualitative only). Q4: not addressed (no confidence calibration or quality head). Q5: suggests a cheap, parameter-light core change (fixed feedback, 1-3 constants) that can be tested within 12 GB without new training of a large readout.
candidate_node_change: Node: dynamics/state of the FlyVis core - add an S1/S2-style background-motion feedback: pool T4/T5 (or HS-like wide-field sum) over the crop, delay it with a Gamma kernel (re-tuned to 30 Hz, e.g. 1-3 frames), and subtract it as a gain or additive term at the photoreceptor/L1-L2 stage on the next step, so the crop-induced and background motion is cancelled before T4/T5 and the readout sees mainly independently moving objects. Only the feedback constant(s) are learned or swept (1-3 parameters). Controls (rule 6.16): (1) stand without the change; (2) the same feedback computed without FlyVis - frame-difference global motion estimate from the raw crop subtracted at the readout input of variant B; (3) stock FlyVis (variant C) with and without the feedback, same readout, same observations and histories. Minimal check (before HOTA): on the existing Z13 loss-episode set, measure (a) ratio of FlyVis output energy on the target box vs neighbouring boxes and (b) share of useful centre corrections in the top 1% confidence (currently 7 of 37 known), for feedback constant sweep {0, small, medium} with one seed and 500 steps as in prior pilots. Stop condition (proposal, to be recorded before the run): if (3) does not exceed (2) on useful-centre share by a pre-registered margin, or target/neighbour ratio does not improve over a=0, stop this implementation and record the failing node (likely: similar neighbours move like the target, so background-motion feedback cannot separate them). Expected weakness: the change addresses background clutter, not identity among similar movers, so its prior chance of helping Z13 is low.
strongest_objection: These papers solve a different problem: detecting tiny (1-15 px) movers against clutter at 240-1000 Hz with hand-tuned filters, reported on 3-6 real clips with ROC curves read from plots and no seeds or intervals. Our failure is choosing the previous target among similar, similarly moving neighbours and refusing when it is gone, inside a crop that already centres the object, at 30 Hz. Background-motion feedback suppresses things that move like the background; neighbouring cars or pedestrians move like the target, so the mechanism is unlikely to change the Z13 decision, and the only identity-like mechanism (S3 trace SD) needs ~200 samples and rejects only static look-alikes.
evidence_strength: S1: preprint v1 with IEEE TNNLS header; journal version not confirmed [uncertain]; no code found; single group, no independent replication; weak-moderate. S2: peer-reviewed (Frontiers in Neurorobotics 2022), mathematical analysis plus small empirical evaluation (3 real videos), no code; weak-moderate. S3: peer-reviewed IEEE TNNLS, code linked on GitHub (not opened), public STNS dataset, clear ablation (Table II); moderate for its narrow claim (rejecting static fake features), weak for tracking. Overall for our decision: weak - same research group, self-comparisons against own earlier STMD models, no learned or tracker baselines, no identity, occlusion or absence tests.
